# jobs


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

abhyasa does slow work in the background: it looks for sources, makes a
walk from a link or a goal, files a folder, plans a course, and writes
the notebook of a step. Each such job has one row here. A row has a
`kind`, a `state` (`running`, `done`, `failed`, `stopped` or `closed`),
a [`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#said) line,
the `start` and `end` times, a `title`, and a `url`: the page of its
object.

The rows are on one document of the learning shelf, so they survive a
restart. The pool future of a job stays in memory; the row is the truth
for the pages. At a start, each row that still says `running` becomes
`closed`: no job lives across a restart.

The rows live on the learning shelf of the vault, next to the concepts
and the walks.

## The row

`ENDED` are the states of a job that does not run. `FRESH` is how long
an ended job shows in the activity chip, until you open its page. `KEEP`
is how long an ended row stays at all.

The rows are the meta of one document. Its text never changes, so a
write changes only the meta.

## Start, end, and a pool job

[`job_start`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/jobs.html#job_start)
writes a running row. `obj` is the object of the job, such as
`walk:<id>` or `course:<id>`; its page marks the end as seen. `quiet`
keeps a job out of the chip, such as the research of a side walk of a
talk.
[`job_end`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/jobs.html#job_end)
closes it.

*Note that the job `key` of `kind` runs now, with its `title`, its

`url` of its page and its object `obj`.*

[`track`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/jobs.html#track) gives a
pool future its row: running now, then `done` or `failed` when it ends.
`ok` maps the result to more fields of the row, such as the link of the
walk that the job made.

### track

``` python
def track(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, key:str, fut, kind:str, ok:NoneType=None, why:NoneType=None, **kw
):
```

*Start the row `key` of the pool future `fut`, and end it when `fut`
ends: `ok(result)` gives more fields, `why(error)` the line of a
failure. Return `fut`.*

A job that runs long says what it does now.
[`Said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/jobs.html#said) is the
state of one pool job, and a new
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#said) goes to
its row too, so a page that reads the row sees the step.

## Seen, closed, and the activity

Opening the page of an object marks its ended jobs as seen. At a start
of the app, a row that says `running` has no job any more: it becomes
`closed`.

<a

``` python

    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, obj:str
)->int:
```

*Mark each ended job of the object `obj` as seen. Return the count that
changed.*

[`activity`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/jobs.html#activity)
is what the chip lists: each job that runs, then each ended job that is
`done`, `failed` or `closed`, not seen, and less than `FRESH` old. A job
that you stopped is not news. A quiet job never shows.

## Tests

A temporary vault for the tests.

``` python
from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
```

A job starts with a running row and no end; the row is in the chip.

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
r = job_start(lr, 'walk:w1:research', 'research', title='Softmax', said='Finding sources', url='/w/w1#sources', obj='walk:w1')
test_eq((r.state, r.end, r.key), ('running', None, 'walk:w1:research'))
test_eq([x.key for x in activity(lr)], ['walk:w1:research'])
test_eq(chip_words(activity(lr)), '1 running')
```

Its end is news until you open the walk.

``` python
v = job_version()
job_end(lr, 'walk:w1:research', said='2 of 3 ideas have a source')
assert job_version() > v
test_eq(chip_words(activity(lr)), 'Ready: Softmax')
test_eq(seen_jobs(lr, 'walk:w1'), 1)
test_eq(activity(lr), [])
```

An old end and a quiet job do not show; a job that you stopped is not
news.

``` python
job_start(lr, 'k2', 'build', title='Old'); job_end(lr, 'k2')
test_eq(activity(lr, now=time.time() + FRESH + 1), [])
job_start(lr, 'k3', 'research', title='Talk', quiet=True)
job_start(lr, 'k4', 'research', title='Mine'); job_end(lr, 'k4', 'stopped')
test_eq([x.key for x in activity(lr)], ['k2'])   # k2 is new now; k3 is quiet and k4 was stopped
test_eq(job_end(lr, 'nope'), None)
```

A restart closes each running row, and the chip says so.

``` python
job_start(lr, 'k5', 'build', title='Diffusion')
test_eq(close_jobs(lr), 2)   # k3 and k5
test_eq(lr.job('k5').state, 'closed')
test_eq(chip_words(activity(lr)), 'Stopped: Diffusion and 1 more')
```

[`track`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/jobs.html#track) ends
the row of a pool future: `done` with the fields of `ok`, or `failed`
with the line of `why`.

``` python
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
```

``` python
pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(1)
track(lr, 'b1', pool.submit(lambda: 'w9'), 'build', ok=lambda jid: dict(url=f'/w/{jid}', obj=f'walk:{jid}'), title='A link').result()
pool.shutdown(wait=True)
test_eq((lr.job('b1').state, lr.job('b1').url, lr.job('b1').obj), ('done', '/w/w9', 'walk:w9'))
pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(1)
f = track(lr, 'b2', pool.submit(lambda: 1 / 0), 'build', why=lambda e: 'No walk.', title='Bad')
pool.shutdown(wait=True)
test_eq((lr.job('b2').state, lr.job('b2').why), ('failed', 'No walk.'))
```

A new line of a running job goes to its row.

``` python
job_start(lr, 'b3', 'build', title='Paper', said='Reading the paper…')
st = Said(lr, 'b3', said='Reading the paper…')
st.update(said='Reading 2 of 3 pages…')
test_eq((st.said, lr.job('b3').said), ('Reading 2 of 3 pages…', 'Reading 2 of 3 pages…'))
```

An ended row older than `KEEP` goes at the next change.

``` python
lr.put_job('b2', end=time.time() - KEEP - 1)
lr.put_job('b3', said='Reading 3 of 3 pages…')
assert lr.job('b2') is None and lr.job('b3') is not None
```
